latestTerminalSummary:
EFFECTIVE_MODEL: [MiniMax M3.1 Flash (Preview) via acpRegistry harness, settings=thinkingEffort xhigh as requested by owner, runtimeMode=full-access, interactionMode=plan | evidence: REQUESTED = mcode MiniMax M3.1 Flash thinkingEffort=xhigh; CONFIGURED = `m:minimax:MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview:v:thinking` per runtime_info, thread-local; CONFIRMED = provider-served identity and effort remain UNVERIFIED — no upstream attestation obtained. I did not verify model identity or that xhigh effort was actually applied, and I make no claim of family diversity versus the opencode critic. Plan mode + full-access is instruction-based restraint, not an enforced read-only sandbox; I verified non-mutation empirically instead of asserting it.]

VERDICT: pass

BLOCKERS: none

SUGGESTIONS:
- `skill_lens/core/config.py:401-410` and `skill_lens/core/config.py:436-443` — the missing-frontmatter predicate is implemented twice in `is_loadable_for_agent`; the second block is unreachable because the first already returns for OpenCode and INVALID otherwise. Confirmed by inspection only (not mutation-proved), so non-blocking.
- `skill_lens/core/resolver.py:850` — the unverified-root note interpolates `c.hit.entrypoint_path` (the skill entrypoint, e.g. `~/.agents/skills/qs`) while the message says "Search root"; the actual root is `~/.agents/skills`. Cosmetic mislabel. Separately, one unknown root emits two near-duplicate notes (`:850` and `:862-864`) for the same path. Verified by reproduction: two "unverified" notes for a single Qoder `.agents/skills` copy.
- `skill_lens/core/resolver.py:210` — `_load_disabled_overrides` remains but is now unused by product code; `tests/test_phase2_gate.py` patches it with a `side_effect` guard that proves it is never called. Harmless retained API, worth a note that it is legacy-only.
- `skill_lens/core/config.py:1015` / `:1092` / `:1114` — the Codex and OMP `qualification` strings ("Disabled via Codex [[skills.config]]", "Disabled via frontmatter enabled: false") are computed but never surfaced: `skill_lens/core/resolver.py:508-511` returns `qualification` only when it contains the substring `"Denied"`, otherwise it collapses to the generic `"Disabled by agent configuration override."` So the per-hit control distinctions exist in the data but not in user-facing reasons. Reproduced for both Codex and OMP. Non-blocking — the state and permission are correct — but the distinct-reason intent in ledger item E is only realized for OpenCode `deny`.
- `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:1684` — the incidental-file assertion was relaxed from `assert res_incidental.found is False` to `found is False or UNSEARCHED`, weakening a prior-stage Stage C contract. The comment justifies it (OpenCode/other roots may legitimately index the file), and I confirmed the semantic claim holds, but this is a deliberate loosening of an accepted stage's test rather than a behavior change the diff explains elsewhere.
- Two trailing spaces on wrapped Rich snapshot lines in `tests/fixtures/snapshots/doctor_findings.txt:7` and `doctor_markup_is_literal.txt:7` are pinned rendering output produced by the message-width change. Do not trim or regenerate blindly.
- The new per-hit fields `loadability`, `invocation`, and `permission` are JSON/model-only: `skill_lens/render.py` and `skill_lens/tui/*` reference none of them. Correct for a presentation-free Stage D, but the TUI cannot yet show the loadability/invocation distinctions the JSON carries.
- `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:1133` and `:1488` — Pi lookup names changed (`"SKILL"`→`"pi_skill"`, `"standalone"`→`"standalone_skill"`) to follow Pi's `frontmatter_name` identity. Correct against upstream, but these edits mean the old directory-name lookup paths for Pi are no longer covered by those assertions.

FILES_AT_RISK:
- `skill_lens/core/config.py` (new, 1119 lines) — load-bearing for all parity, redaction, and loadability behavior. Reviewed end to end.
- `skill_lens/core/resolver.py` — `_candidates_for` gating, `_reason` qualification handling, truncation disclosure with `display_paths`/`_lexical_display` fallbacks, restored `__all__`.
- `skill_lens/core/discovery.py` — three independent depth caps (4/16/32) and `_record_truncation`; exact-cap leaf inspection is the most delicate new logic.
- `skill_lens/core/snapshot.py` + `skill_lens/core/snapshot_models.py` — `resolved_controls` capture and the frozen-navigation purity contract.
- `skill_lens/core/doctor.py` — loadability-aware frontmatter findings and the new `depth_limit_truncated` WARNING.
- `skill_lens/registry/agents/{opencode,pi,qoder,omp,grok,windsurf,antigravity,claude}.toml` — rank, `identity_source`, and `loadability` changes are behavior-affecting.
- `skill_lens/core/health.py` — `missing_frontmatter` split that doctor and `is_loadable_for_agent` both depend on.
- `tests/test_stage_d_repairs.py` (2142 lines, 63 tests) and the four modified pre-existing test files plus three golden/snapshot fixtures.
- Not modified but verified as load-bearing and unchanged: `skill_lens/cli.py`, `render.py`, `scanner.py`, `compare.py`, `diff.py`, `exitcodes.py`, `paths.py`, `parser.py`, `registry/loader.py` (only an additive `loadability` field).

CONCEDED:
- Gates are green as recorded and I reproduced a consistent subset myself: 63/63 Stage D tests and 168 passed + 1 skipped across the four modified legacy test files, all with `--no-cov` and an external cache dir. I did not re-run the full 922-test coverage gate myself; I relied on the coordinator log for that number and did not independently confirm the 90.50% coverage figure.
- All 13 mutation controls are genuine. I recomputed SHA-256 for each mutated file against the working tree — all match `original_hash` and `restored_hash` — and confirmed clean/mutant/restored `0/1/0`. I read the two most load-bearing mutant logs and they show the intended assertion failures, not incidental errors. This proves those 13 guards; it is not an exhaustive mutation score, and I do not claim one.
- I read the complete-product-test diff and the actual files and consumers behind it rather than the diff alone, and I read both round-one reports plus the adjudication. Where the ledger's claims were checkable I reproduced them; where they were not (e.g. claims about specific vendor doc strings) I fetched the primary sources.
- Ledger items A–J and both resumed boundary controls all reproduce. Codex symlink parity (A), the disabled_overrides API split (B), doctor portability (C), unknown retained roots (D), OpenCode invocation/deny (E), config extent and layer ordering (F), depth-cap disclosure (G), non-target nested coexistence (H), bounded disclosure (I), and redaction (J) each passed independent reproduction. I also confirmed late-arrival/late-deletion capture-time immutability, custom-agent loader/API compatibility, full captured-path coverage for all ten agents, captured-control immutability, and legacy snapshot fallback.
- Ledger item B's rejected half stays rejected. I verified the second half directly: an OpenCode shell-deny rule leaves permission `allow`, matching the documented base wildcard allow and the adjudication's narrowing. I did not reintroduce the unconditional-unmatched-ask claim.
- The residual limitations are real and I state them rather than papering over them: served model identity and effort are unverified; full-access/plan restraint is instruction-based, though I empirically confirmed `git status -uall` is byte-identical to the recorded pre-review status, so this review made zero repository writes.
- Vendor-doc cross-check: I fetched the OpenCode V2 skills and config pages and the Pi `skills.ts` source directly rather than trusting the evidence table. Every load-bearing claim I sampled checks out — path-derived IDs (including literal ID `SKILL` for a root-level `SKILL.md`, which I reproduced), later-registered-source precedence, the current-directory-to-filesystem-root merge order, all-frontmatter-optional with description gating advertisement, and Pi's `frontmatterName || parentDirName`, user-before-project load order, and stop-at-`SKILL.md` traversal. One OpenCode doc string cited in round one as absent does appear in the current page ("A root-level `SKILL.md` currently has the literal ID `SKILL` in V2"), which corroborates rather than contradicts the implementation's ID behavior.
